A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LocAgent and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. Content can be reliably matched across the changed pagination and numbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original localization experiments on SWE-Bench-Lite and Loc-Bench, component and graph-format ablations, and downstream bug-repair results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical experiments and reports revised Loc-Bench results.

M1.justification: The heterogeneous graph, sparse indexes, three retrieval tools, agent planning, consistency-based ranking, and model fine-tuning procedure are unchanged. The added graph-method comparison does not introduce a new LocAgent component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Python code localization on SWE-Bench-Lite and Loc-Bench, including bug reports, feature requests, security and performance issues, plus downstream bug repair. The reduced Loc-Bench sample count does not establish changed task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged in the localization, efficiency, downstream-repair, and graph-format experiments. V2's new Table 1 compares graph-method characteristics; it does not add those systems to the empirical evaluations.

E3.justification: Loc-Bench's reported size decreases from 660 to 560 examples, with all four category counts revised (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3). The selection rationale is not supplied. Metrics and SWE-Bench-Lite's 274-example protocol remain unchanged; Section 5.7 also clarifies the file-count range as 1–5, whose endpoints already appear in v1 Figure 8.

E4.justification: Figure 5 updates the category-wise localization analysis for the revised Loc-Bench sample. V1 Appendix B.2 and its distributions of patched-file, module, and function counts are removed. The tool ablations, hop-distance analysis, and appendix graph-format experiment are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides changed seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results continue to use point estimates without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Loc-Bench scores are replaced under the changed sample: LocAgent with Claude-3.5 changes from 84.59 to 83.39 file Acc@5 and from 62.10 to 60.71 function Acc@15 (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 7). Figure 5 also changes. These are not same-setting performance losses; SWE-Bench-Lite, efficiency, ablation, NDCG, and downstream-repair scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph definition in Section 3.1 and graph-distance expression in Appendix C.1.2 are unchanged. No new assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about graph-guided localization, Loc-Bench, inexpensive fine-tuned models, and downstream repair benefits. The headline 92.7% localization accuracy, approximately 86% cost reduction, and 12% Pass@10 improvement are retained.

C2.justification: New Section 2.3 adds comparative explanations involving MCTS traversal overhead, dependence on Cypher-query capability, and missing structural relationships in other graph systems. These expand the rationale for LocAgent's representation and traversal choices. Existing empirical interpretations and the Limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.5 newly documents pricing sources and rates underlying existing cost estimates: $0.20 per million input/output tokens for Qwen2.5-32B, and $0.14 input/$0.28 output for Qwen2.5-7B. This is additional disclosure; training settings, implementation details, prompts, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 and Table 1 substantially expand positioning against closely related graph systems. They discuss Aider's RepoMap, RepoGraph, CodexGraph, RepoUnderstander, and the already-cited OrcaLoca, explicitly comparing represented relationships, node types, and traversal strategies.

P1.justification: V2 adds a related-work subsection, lightly rewrites Section 5.7, standardizes some headings, and removes the introductory dataset-count sentence and Appendix B.2. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the graph-method comparison table and removes v1's dataset-distribution Figure 8. Existing figures and tables shift within the layout and are renumbered where necessary; the prompt figure is retained as Figure 8 instead of Figure 9.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparison with closely related graph methods improves research positioning, and the pricing footnote makes the cost claims more transparent. These are limited gains, tempered by the unexplained Loc-Bench reduction and removal of its distribution plots, which reduce dataset transparency. The method and principal SWE-Bench-Lite evidence remain unchanged.
